title: Using ChatGPT as a Lesson Planning Assistant with Preservice Secondary Mathematics Teachers
extended_summary:
This qualitative study examines how preservice secondary mathematics teachers used ChatGPT as a lesson-planning assistant during a methods course microteaching assignment. The authors focus on two related questions: how PSTs reacted to ChatGPT’s mathematical solutions and what they found useful or not useful when using ChatGPT to plan a mini-lesson.

Participants first solved their assigned mathematics task independently, then prompted ChatGPT to solve the same task and to generate aims/objectives for a lesson based on that task. They reflected on the chatbot’s output, revised their plans, and continued using ChatGPT informally while developing their mini-lessons. The study took place in two sections of a secondary mathematics methods course at a public urban university in the northeastern United States, with 22 PSTs total (mostly undergraduates, plus graduate career changers).

Findings show that ChatGPT was often inaccurate on mathematical tasks, especially when the problems required careful interpretation or domain-specific reasoning. PSTs were usually able to judge pedagogical output as repetitive or teacher-centered, but they frequently failed to recognize mathematical errors and sometimes treated incorrect answers as merely alternative approaches. For planning, ChatGPT was most useful as a starting point for ideas, objectives, misconceptions, and assessment suggestions, but PSTs generally did not adopt its output unchanged. The authors conclude that teacher preparation should emphasize critical reflection and AI literacy, especially a framework for evaluating mathematical correctness and pedagogical quality when using generative AI in lesson planning.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot / large language model assistant used for text generation, question answering, and planning support.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by preservice secondary mathematics teachers as a lesson-planning assistant and to solve the same mathematics tasks the PSTs were assigned during microteaching planning.

findings.finding_summary: In this qualitative study with n=22 PSTs (19 included in the math-output analysis), ChatGPT's mathematical responses were correct in 6 of 19 coded instances. PSTs were generally accurate in judging pedagogical output as teacher-centered and repetitive, but were often inaccurate when judging incorrect mathematical output, frequently treating wrong solutions as merely a 'different approach.'
findings.measure: Correctness of ChatGPT mathematical solutions; PST accuracy in evaluating ChatGPT output; reflective judgments about pedagogical usefulness

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative study using deductive coding of PST reflections and ChatGPT outputs rather than an experimental design. It provides useful descriptive evidence, but causal claims about effects on planning quality or instruction are not supported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests mixed practical value: ChatGPT sometimes supported idea generation and planning, but also produced incorrect mathematics and teacher-centered lesson ideas. No effect size is reported, so impact appears modest and uncertain.
